name: Golf
description: Golf is a card game for two or more players where the object is to score as little as possible, like the sport. Each player has a layout of face-down cards that can be replaced by drawing from stock or discard piles. The game is commonly played over 9 or 18 deals ('holes'), with the lowest total score winning. Also known as Polish Polka, Polish Poker, Turtle (4-card), Hara Kiri (6-card), or Crazy Nines (9-card).

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: USA/UK
Time Period: Early-to-mid 20th century
Creator(s): Unknown (folk game)
Etymology: Named after the sport of golf where lower scores are better; scores represent 'strokes' taken to play a hole
timeline: Early 20th Century: Game first appears in card-playing communities
Mid 20th Century: Spreads throughout North America and Britain
Late 20th Century: Multiple variations develop (4-card, 6-card, 8-card, etc.)
Modern Era: Remains popular as a casual family game; digital versions available
history.cultural: Golf is a widespread casual game in North America and Britain, often played in families and social gatherings. Despite its popularity, it is seldom found in card game books. The game has many alternative names including Polish Polka, Polish Poker, Turtle, Hara Kiri, and Crazy Nines depending on the number of cards used.
history.evolution: Golf started as a simple 4-card layout game and evolved into multiple variations with different numbers of cards (4, 6, 8, 9, 10). The 6-card version with face-up replacement cards became particularly popular. Various scoring variations and special rules (like power cards in Cambio/Cabo) have been added over time.

setup.players:
Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 8 (use 2 decks for 8+ players)
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: No
setup.deck:
Type: Standard 52-card
Number of Decks: 1 (2 for 8+ players)
Jokers: Optional (variations)
setup.dealing:
4-Card Golf: 4 cards each, arranged in square, 2 face-up to view
6-Card Golf: 6 cards each, arranged 2x3, some variations start with all face down
8-Card Golf: 8 cards each
Remaining cards form stock pile; top card turned for discard pile
setup.equipment:
Standard deck of cards
Score sheet for tracking over multiple holes

rules.objective: Have the lowest scoring layout at the end of each hole (hand). Play 9 or 18 holes; lowest cumulative score wins.
rules.gameplay:
FOUR-CARD GOLF:
1. Players arrange 4 cards face down in square; view 2 nearest cards once
2. Player left of dealer starts
3. On your turn, either: - Draw from stock, optionally replace a layout card (discard replaced card) - Take top discard, must use to replace layout card - Knock (ends play after others take one more turn)
4. Cannot look at layout cards before deciding which to replace
5. If you look at a face-down card, you must replace it SIX-CARD GOLF:
1. 6 cards arranged 2x3, usually all face down initially
2. Draw and replace as in 4-card
3. Replacement cards placed face up
4. Play ends when one player has all cards face up
keyRules: You cannot look at your face-down cards before deciding which to replace
If you draw from stock, you may discard it without using it
If you take the discard, you must use it to replace a card
In 6-card, play ends when one player has all cards face up
Looking at a face-down card forces you to replace it

strategy.basic:
For Beginners:
1. Remember the two cards you viewed at the start
2. Replace high cards (10s, 9s, 8s) with lower cards
3. Kings (0 points) are valuable - keep them
4. Don't knock unless you think you have the lowest score
strategy.intermediate:
1. Track which cards have been discarded to know what's available
2. Consider the risk of drawing vs taking a known discard
3. In 6-card, watch which cards opponents are turning face up
4. Try to create pairs in columns for zero scoring
strategy.advanced:
1. Calculate probabilities of drawing useful cards
2. Bluff by knocking with a higher score to pressure opponents
3. Memorize all visible cards to deduce opponent holdings
4. Endgame calculation when few cards remain in stock
tips: Don't forget what your initial two cards were - you can't look at them again
Sometimes it's better to keep a face-down card unknown rather than risk replacing it with something worse
Watch the discard pile - taking a known card is often safer than drawing
In 6-card, ending the game quickly can prevent opponents from improving

variations.name: Four-Card Golf
variations.description: Each player has four cards in a square, two of which may be looked at once before play. Player may knock to end the hand after others get one more turn. Also known as Turtle.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Final hand size is set above; no other overrides needed.

variations.name: Six-Card Golf
variations.description: Six cards per player in a 2x3 layout. Replacement cards are placed face up. Play ends when any player has all six cards face up; others get one more turn. Also known as Hara Kiri.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Final hand size is set above; no other overrides needed.

variations.name: Eight-Card Golf
variations.description: Eight cards per player; layout and play similar to six-card. Play ends when one player's layout is fully face up.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Final hand size is set above; no other overrides needed.

variations.name: Nine-Card Golf
variations.description: Nine cards in a 3x3 grid. Same draw-and-replace flow; play ends when any player has all cards face up. Three of a kind in a column score zero. Also known as Crazy Nines.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Final hand size is set above; no other overrides needed.

variations.name: Ten-Card Golf
variations.description: Ten cards per player; less common. Same draw-and-replace mechanic; end condition typically when one player's layout is fully face up.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Final hand size is set above; no other overrides needed.

variations.name: Golf with Power Cards
variations.description: Four-card Golf variant (Cambio, Cabo, Pablo, Cactus, Dacz) where certain cards drawn from the stock grant special powers (peek at a card, swap with opponent, etc.); used or discarded as normal if taken from the discard pile.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Power-card behaviour is custom logic; no single engine constant captures it.

variations.name: Single-deck Golf
variations.description: Played with one deck for two to four players. Rules match the chosen layout (e.g. four-card or six-card); sometimes jokers are not used.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Deck count is a table setting; not an engine constant override.

variations.name: Knocking variant
variations.description: In four-card style, a player may knock instead of drawing to end the hand; each other player gets one final turn. Knocker may be penalised if not lowest, or rewarded if lowest (e.g. score zero).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Knock timing and penalties are rule variants, not engine constants.

scoring.description: Layout is turned face-up at end of play. Numeral cards score face value (Ace=1, Two=2, etc.), Jack and Queen score 10 each, King scores zero. Lowest cumulative score after 9 or 18 deals wins.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest total score after 9 or 18 holes (deals) wins.
